newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Bernheim-Comofi books provision, holds div.
newsitem.headline: Bernheim-Comofi books provision, holds div.

text.p: Belgian property group Bernheim-Comofi is booking a 375 million Belgian franc provision in 1996 accounts and holding 1996 dividend to cover expected losses from its five-year-old foray into the Berlin property market.

The provision, which was to cover expected past and future charges linked to its Berlin operation, would "weigh heavily on the group's consolidated accounts in 1996," the group warned in a statement released late on Thursday.
"In this context the board will propose to shareholders the payment of an unchanged dividend," it said.

"The enthusiasm generated by the renovation of Berlin led to an unprecedented construction boom, while the expected arrival of the German federal government was delayed. This double effect has created a property surplus, which has had a negative impact on the level of rents," Bernheim-Comofi said.
The Belgian company teamed up with Opus, a unit of German property company Wayss & Freytag, in 1991 to develop a site in Berlin's Rosenthaler Strasse.
The plan was to build a 22,000 square metre office complex, complete with 2,000 square metres of shops and 6,000 square metres of apartments.
